pinyin: yǐ zǐ zhī máo, gōng zǐ zhī dùn
literal: with · your · spear · attack · your · shield
natural: use your own spear against your own shield

meaning.en: To refute someone with the logic of his own words or methods, exposing his self-contradiction.
meaning.zh: 用对方自己的说法或方法来反驳对方，使其自相矛盾。

equivalents: turn his own argument against him

examples.zh: 辩论时，他以子之矛，攻子之盾，对手哑口无言。
examples.en: In the debate he turned his opponent's own argument against him, leaving him speechless.

examples.zh: 你说诚信重要，自己却失信，我只能以子之矛攻子之盾了。
examples.en: You say honesty is vital, yet broke your word; I can only use your own words against you.

examples.zh: 以子之矛，攻子之盾，这是最有力的反驳。
examples.en: Using your own spear against your own shield is the strongest rebuttal.

story.en: A man sold spears and shields, boasting that his spear could pierce anything and his shield nothing could pierce. Someone asked: 'What if I use your spear against your shield?' and he could not answer.
story.zh: 楚人有鬻盾与矛者，誉之曰：“吾盾之坚，物莫能陷也。”又誉其矛曰：“吾矛之利，于物无不陷也。”或曰：“以子之矛，陷子之盾，何如？”其人弗能应也。

date.en: end of Warring States, 3rd c. BC

usage.en: From the 矛盾 fable; used in debate and argument. Neutral, a tactic rather than praise or blame. Also found without the comma.
usage.zh: 出自“矛盾”寓言；用于辩论。中性，指一种反驳手法。也可不加逗号连写。

natural: treat a big topic as a small one

meaning.en: To treat an important matter too lightly or superficially; the opposite of making a fuss over nothing.
meaning.zh: 对重大的问题只作轻描淡写的处理。

examples.zh: 这么严重的事故，不能大题小做，必须彻查。
examples.en: An accident this serious can't be played down; it must be thoroughly investigated.

examples.zh: 领导对质量问题大题小做，引起了员工不满。
examples.en: Management brushed off the quality problem and the staff were unhappy.

examples.zh: 写论文大题小做，会显得内容空泛。
examples.en: Treating a big topic lightly in a thesis makes the content seem thin.

usage.en: The opposite of 小题大做; criticises underestimating matters. Common in essays and exam writing. Predicate.
usage.zh: 与“小题大做”相反，批评把重要的事看轻。常见于议论文和写作。作谓语。

natural: not found in the classics or commentaries

meaning.en: Not recorded in the authoritative books; hence obscure or little-known.
meaning.zh: 经典著作中没有记载，指没有名气，或没有根据。

examples.zh: 这位不见经传的小作家，一部小说却火了。
examples.en: This little-known writer suddenly became popular with a single novel.

examples.zh: 他的观点不见经传，难以服人。
examples.en: His view has no basis in the authorities and is hard to take seriously.

examples.zh: 决赛中，一支不见经传的小队击败了冠军。
examples.en: In the final an unknown little team beat the champions.

usage.en: Usually attributive, as in 不见经传的人物. It is about being obscure, not necessarily bad; the person or idea is unrecorded. Also 名不见经传 is the more usual set form.
usage.zh: 多作定语，如“不见经传的人物”。强调默默无闻，不一定不好。也常用“名不见经传”。

natural: can be reached in one step

meaning.en: Can be achieved at a single stroke, with no sustained effort; usually used in the negative.
meaning.zh: 一下子就能达到，多用于否定，表示事情不是一下子能成功的。

examples.zh: 学外语绝非一蹴可几，需要长期积累。
examples.en: Learning a foreign language can't be done overnight; it takes long accumulation.

examples.zh: 成功不是一蹴可几的事。
examples.en: Success isn't something achieved in a single step.

examples.zh: 改革的任务艰巨，岂是一蹴可几？
examples.en: The task of reform is arduous; how could it be done in one step?

usage.en: Nearly always negative (不是/岂是/绝非一蹴可几). 几 here is jī ('reach, near'). Compare 一蹴而就.
usage.zh: 几乎总是用于否定（“不是/岂是/绝非一蹴可几”）。“几”读jī（达到、接近）。可与“一蹴而就”比较。

natural: staring wide-eyed from behind

meaning.en: To be far behind and unable to catch up, just staring after the leader.
meaning.zh: 在后面干瞪眼，赶不上，形容远远落后。

equivalents: can only gawp at someone's back

examples.zh: 他的速度太快，其他选手只能瞠乎其后。
examples.en: He was so fast that the other runners could only stare after him.

examples.zh: 在这个领域，我们还瞠乎其后，必须加快追赶。
examples.en: In this field we are far behind and must speed up to catch up.

examples.zh: 她的成绩让同学们瞠乎其后。
examples.en: Her results left her classmates trailing far behind.

story.en: Yan Hui told Confucius: 'When you run like lightning, leaving no dust, I can only stare behind you' (夫子奔逸绝尘，而回瞠若乎后矣).
story.zh: 颜回说：“夫子步亦步，夫子趋亦趋，夫子驰亦驰，夫子奔逸绝尘，而回瞠若乎后矣。”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Usually describes being left behind in a race or field of work; note it sounds literary. 瞠 means 'stare'.
usage.zh: 形容在竞争或工作中远远落后；带书面色彩。“瞠”意为瞪眼看。

pinyin: lǎo wáng mài guā —— zì mài zì kuā
literal: old · Wang · sell · melon — self · sell · self · boast
natural: Old Wang sells melons and praises his own

meaning.en: A seller praises his own goods; someone who boasts about himself or his own work.
meaning.zh: 卖瓜的人夸自己的瓜好，比喻自己夸自己。

examples.zh: 不是我老王卖瓜，自卖自夸，这个方案确实好。
examples.en: I'm not blowing my own trumpet, but the plan really is good.

examples.zh: 他一开口就是老王卖瓜，让人听着不舒服。
examples.en: As soon as he opened his mouth it was self-praise, which made people uncomfortable.

examples.zh: 老王卖瓜，自卖自夸，他的话只能听一半。
examples.en: He praises his own goods, so only half of what he says is worth hearing.

usage.en: Often used as a self-mocking preface before praising something of one's own. Also said as 王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸.
usage.zh: 常作自嘲式开场，用在夸自己的东西之前。也说“王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸”。

natural: a single word can make a nation flourish

meaning.en: A single wise remark can bring prosperity to a country.
meaning.zh: 一句话就能使国家兴盛，形容话语的重要作用。

equivalents: a word that makes a nation
one saying can change a country

examples.zh: 古人说一言兴邦，一言丧邦，领导人的话十分重要。
examples.en: The ancients said that one word can raise or ruin a nation; leaders' words matter greatly.

examples.zh: 一言兴邦的传说，说明了进谏的作用。
examples.en: Legends of the word that raised a state show the value of remonstrance.

examples.zh: 他的发言被认为是一言兴邦之论。
examples.en: His speech was regarded as an utterance that could make a nation thrive.

story.en: Duke Ding asked whether one saying could make a state flourish. Confucius replied that no saying could do that exactly, but there is one close to it: 'Being a ruler is hard' (为君难，为臣不易).
story.zh: 鲁定公问：“一言而可以兴邦，有诸？”孔子对曰：“言不可以若是其几也。人之言曰：‘为君难，为臣不易。’”

usage.en: Often paired with 一言丧邦. Formal; used of statements by leaders or thinkers, sometimes ironic about empty slogans.
usage.zh: 常与“一言丧邦”连用。较书面，多指领导者或思想家的话，有时讽刺空洞口号。

natural: beat the oar in midstream

meaning.en: To swear a resolve to restore the country or to fulfil a great ambition.
meaning.zh: 在江心敲击船桨发誓，形容收复失地、实现壮志的决心。

equivalents: vow to achieve a great cause

examples.zh: 祖逖北伐，击楫中流，誓言收复中原。
examples.en: Zu Ti led the northern campaign, beating his oar in midstream and swearing to retake the Central Plains.

examples.zh: 他击楫中流，立志为国家奋斗终身。
examples.en: He swore a vow, as if beating his oar mid-river, to dedicate his life to his country.

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，同学们仿佛击楫中流，意气风发。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the students seemed to be vowing great deeds, full of spirit.

story.en: Zu Ti led an army north across the Yangtze, beat the oar in midstream and swore: 'If I fail to clear the Central Plains, may I be like this river and never return' (中流击楫而誓曰).
story.zh: 祖逖率兵北伐，渡江中流，击楫而誓曰：“祖逖不能清中原而复济者，有如大江！”

usage.en: Heroic and literary; the subject is usually a patriot or reformer. Allusion to General Zu Ti.
usage.zh: 豪壮的书面语，主语多为爱国者或改革者。典出祖逖。

literal: firewood · used up · fire · passed on
natural: the firewood burns out but the fire is passed on

meaning.en: Knowledge, a cause or a tradition is passed from one generation to the next without end.
meaning.zh: 木柴烧尽，火种还在传下去，比喻学问、事业或技艺代代相传。

examples.zh: 老匠人把手艺传给徒弟，薪尽火传。
examples.en: The old craftsman passed his skills on to his apprentice, so the flame is handed on.

examples.zh: 科学事业需要薪尽火传，一代接一代。
examples.en: The cause of science needs to be passed on generation after generation.

examples.zh: 这个剧种薪火相传，至今仍有观众。
examples.en: This form of opera has been handed down and still has an audience today.

story.en: Zhuangzi: 'The fingers use up the firewood, but the fire is passed on, and we cannot know when it ends' (指穷于为薪，火传也，不知其尽也).
story.zh: 《庄子》：“指穷于为薪，火传也，不知其尽也。”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Positive; about inheritance of skills and ideals. The shorter, more modern 薪火相传 is common in news.
usage.zh: 褒义；指技艺、理想的传承。更简短的“薪火相传”在新闻中常见。

natural: use defence as attack

meaning.en: To win the initiative through a defensive stance; defend in such a way that it becomes an offence.
meaning.zh: 用防守的办法来进攻，以守势取得主动。

equivalents: the best defence is a good offence

examples.zh: 面对强敌，教练决定以守为攻，伺机反击。
examples.en: Facing a strong rival the coach chose to defend and wait for a chance to counter-attack.

examples.zh: 他在谈判中以守为攻，耐心等对方露出破绽。
examples.en: In the negotiation he used defence as attack and waited for the other side's slip.

examples.zh: 以守为攻，不是消极防守，而是为了更好的进攻。
examples.en: Attacking through defence isn't passive; it prepares a better attack.

usage.en: Strategy and sport; positive about tactical patience. Predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 多用于战略和体育，赞扬有耐心的战术。作谓语、状语。

natural: the best warfare strikes at the enemy's plans

meaning.en: The best way to wage war is to defeat the enemy's strategy, not to fight him.
meaning.zh: 用兵的上策是挫败敌人的谋略。

equivalents: the best strategy is to thwart the enemy's plans
win by wits, not by force

examples.zh: 上兵伐谋，商场竞争也是如此。
examples.en: The best strategy is to defeat the opponent's plans, and so it is in business.

examples.zh: 他懂得上兵伐谋，不战而屈人之兵。
examples.en: He knows that the highest military art is to attack strategy, and wins without fighting.

examples.zh: 真正的高手上兵伐谋，从不蛮干。
examples.en: True experts win by outwitting rivals, never by brute force.

story.en: Sunzi: 'The best way to use the military is to attack the enemy's plans; next, his alliances; next, his army; the worst, his walled cities' (上兵伐谋，其次伐交，其次伐兵，其下攻城).
story.zh: 《孙子兵法》：“上兵伐谋，其次伐交，其次伐兵，其下攻城。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前5世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 5th c. BC

usage.en: Quoted from the Art of War; next-best are 伐交, 伐兵, 攻城. Praise of strategic thinking in sport, business and politics.
usage.zh: 引自《孙子兵法》；其次是伐交、伐兵、攻城。在体育、商业和政治中赞扬战略思维。

synonyms: 不战而屈人之兵，善之善者也

natural: a crimson heart and green blood

meaning.en: Boundless loyalty and patriotism, even to the point of giving one's life.
meaning.zh: 赤诚的心，为正义而流的血，形容忠诚爱国、不惜牺牲。

examples.zh: 烈士们丹心碧血，换来了今天的和平。
examples.en: The martyrs gave their loyal hearts and blood and bought us today's peace.

examples.zh: 这座纪念碑是为丹心碧血的英雄而建。
examples.en: The monument was built for the heroes of devoted loyalty.

examples.zh: 他一生丹心碧血，从未辜负国家。
examples.en: All his life he was utterly loyal and never let the country down.

usage.en: Solemn, for patriots and martyrs. 碧血 comes from the legend that a loyal man's blood turned jade-green after three years. Not for casual use.
usage.zh: 庄重，用于爱国者、烈士。“碧血”源自忠臣之血三年化碧的传说。不宜轻用。

natural: good for the room, good for the home

meaning.en: A wish that the bride will bring harmony to her new family.
meaning.zh: 新娘能使家庭和顺，常用作婚礼祝福。

equivalents: a blessing on the new household
may she make the home happy

examples.zh: 恭祝新人宜室宜家，白头偕老。
examples.en: We wish the couple a harmonious home and a lifetime together.

examples.zh: 她贤惠能干，真是宜室宜家的好媳妇。
examples.en: She is capable and kind, truly a bride who brings harmony to the household.

examples.zh: 红纸上写着“之子于归，宜室宜家”。
examples.en: The red paper read, 'The bride goes to her new home, and brings harmony to the house.'

story.en: The poem 'Peach Blossoms' sings of a bride: 'The bride goes to her new home; she will be good to her household' (之子于归，宜其室家).
story.zh: 《桃夭》：“桃之夭夭，灼灼其华。之子于归，宜其室家。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: A wedding blessing, traditionally about the bride; now also on gifts and scrolls. Elegant.
usage.zh: 婚礼祝词，传统上指新娘；现也见于礼品和字画。典雅。

natural: melons and melonlets in unbroken succession

meaning.en: A wish that a family's descendants will be many and prosper generation after generation.
meaning.zh: 瓜藤连绵结果，比喻子孙昌盛、世代延续。

examples.zh: 祝您家族瓜瓞绵绵，人丁兴旺。
examples.en: May your family line flourish and increase.

examples.zh: 婚宴上，长辈送上祝福：瓜瓞绵绵。
examples.en: At the wedding banquet the elders offered their blessing: may your descendants be many.

examples.zh: 这幅画画了瓜果满藤，寓意瓜瓞绵绵。
examples.en: The painting shows a vine heavy with melons, symbolising the wish of unbroken descendants.

story.en: The ode 'Mian' begins: 'Unbroken the melon vines' (绵绵瓜瓞), praising how the Zhou people grew from small beginnings to many descendants.
story.zh: 《诗经·大雅·绵》：“绵绵瓜瓞，民之初生，自土沮漆。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: A wish said at weddings and birthdays, often on artworks. 瓞 (dié) is a small melon. Elegant and traditional.
usage.zh: 婚礼、寿辰上的祝福语，常见于书画。“瓞”（dié）指小瓜。典雅传统。

natural: kites fly and fish leap

meaning.en: Everything in nature living freely and happily; also vitality and harmony of heaven and earth.
meaning.zh: 老鹰在天空飞，鱼在水里跳，形容万物各得其所、自由活跃。

examples.zh: 春日的湖边，鸢飞鱼跃，生机盎然。
examples.en: By the lake in spring, kites soar and fish leap, full of life.

examples.zh: 教育应该让孩子像鸢飞鱼跃一样自由成长。
examples.en: Education should let children grow freely, as kites fly and fish leap.

examples.zh: 他向往鸢飞鱼跃的田园生活。
examples.en: He yearns for the free, lively life of the countryside.

story.en: The ode says: 'The kite flies up to heaven, the fish leap in the deep' (鸢飞戾天，鱼跃于渊), later read as a picture of all things finding their place.
story.zh: 《诗经·大雅·旱麓》：“鸢飞戾天，鱼跃于渊。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Literary and poetic; positive. 鸢 (yuān) is a kite, a bird of prey.
usage.zh: 书面语，富有诗意，褒义。“鸢”指老鹰一类猛禽。

natural: turn the eyes and smile

meaning.en: A smile glanced back over the shoulder, charming and alluring.
meaning.zh: 回过头来嫣然一笑，形容女子的妩媚。

equivalents: a backward glance and a smile

examples.zh: 她回眸一笑，全场的人都看呆了。
examples.en: She turned back with a smile and the whole room was spellbound.

examples.zh: 电影里那回眸一笑，成了经典镜头。
examples.en: That backward smile in the film became a classic shot.

examples.zh: 他至今记得她回眸一笑的样子。
examples.en: He still remembers how she smiled looking back.

story.en: Bai Juyi describes Yang Guifei: 'Turning her head with a smile, she shows a hundred charms' (回眸一笑百媚生，六宫粉黛无颜色).
story.zh: 白居易《长恨歌》：“回眸一笑百媚生，六宫粉黛无颜色。”

usage.en: Romantic and literary; the best-known line is 回眸一笑百媚生 from Bai Juyi's Song of Everlasting Sorrow (describing Yang Guifei).
usage.zh: 浪漫，书面语；最著名的诗句是白居易《长恨歌》“回眸一笑百媚生”（写杨贵妃）。

natural: draw a knife to cut water

meaning.en: Doomed to fail: just as water flows on after you cut it, worries cannot be cut away; also sorrows that grow worse when one tries to drown them.
meaning.zh: 拔刀砍水，水仍然流；比喻愁绪无法排解，或徒劳无功。

equivalents: like cutting water with a knife
a sorrow that cannot be severed

examples.zh: 抽刀断水水更流，越想忘记，越是忘不了。
examples.en: Cut the water with a knife and it flows on; the more I try to forget, the less I can.

examples.zh: 想靠禁令根除这种风气，无异于抽刀断水。
examples.en: Trying to stamp out this trend by prohibition is like cutting water with a knife.

examples.zh: 他借酒浇愁，却是抽刀断水。
examples.en: He drowned his sorrows in drink, but it was like cutting water with a knife.

origin.source: 李白《宣州谢朓楼饯别校书叔云》

story.en: Li Bai wrote: 'Draw a knife to cut the water and the water flows on; raise a cup to drown sorrow and the sorrow grows' (抽刀断水水更流，举杯消愁愁更愁).
story.zh: 李白：“抽刀断水水更流，举杯消愁愁更愁。”

usage.en: Poetic. Usually quoted with 举杯消愁愁更愁. Used for sorrow that can't be shaken off and for efforts that achieve nothing.
usage.zh: 富有诗意。常与“举杯消愁愁更愁”连引。指愁绪难解，也指努力徒劳。

natural: a snake's track in the grass, a thread of ash

meaning.en: A faint but traceable clue running through a work, foreshadowing later events; hints that are hidden but unbroken.
meaning.zh: 像蛇在草中爬过、灰线在地上拉过，痕迹隐约可寻；比喻文章中伏笔隐隐、前后呼应。

equivalents: a thread running through the plot

examples.zh: 这部小说草蛇灰线，伏笔埋得极深。
examples.en: The novel's foreshadowing is subtle, with its clues buried deep.

examples.zh: 读《红楼梦》要留意草蛇灰线般的暗示。
examples.en: When reading Dream of the Red Chamber, watch for hints as faint as a snake's trail.

examples.zh: 这部悬疑剧草蛇灰线，每一集都有暗示。
examples.en: The mystery series plants its hints so faintly that every episode carries a clue.

usage.en: Literary criticism (often applied to fiction, drama, plotting); favoured by commentators of classic novels. Praise when the clues cohere.
usage.zh: 文学批评用语，常用于小说、戏剧的情节布局，古典小说评点家喜用。线索连贯时含赞美。

natural: a tiger cub from a general's family

meaning.en: A brave and capable child of a distinguished family; the son who lives up to his father.
meaning.zh: 名将的后代也勇猛能干，指有出息的子女。

equivalents: a chip off the old block
a worthy son of a great father

examples.zh: 他父亲是名将，他自己也是将门虎子。
examples.en: His father was a famous general and he is a worthy son.

examples.zh: 这位新队长是将门虎子，球技出众。
examples.en: The new captain follows in his father's footsteps and is an outstanding player.

examples.zh: 真是将门虎子，小小年纪就胆识过人。
examples.en: A true chip off the old block, so brave at so young an age.

usage.en: Praise for the child of an accomplished parent; uses 虎子 (tiger cub). Also said 将门无犬子 or 将门出虎子.
usage.zh: 夸奖有成就的父母的孩子；“虎子”喻勇猛的儿子。也说“将门无犬子”“将门出虎子”。

natural: emotion running high

meaning.en: Full of deep, passionate emotion; to sing with heroic feeling.
meaning.zh: 情绪激昂，慷慨悲歌；形容心情激动，意气风发。

examples.zh: 他读着《短歌行》，慨当以慷，热泪盈眶。
examples.en: Reading the 'Short Song', he was filled with stirring emotion and his eyes welled with tears.

examples.zh: 宴席上酒酣耳热，众人慨当以慷。
examples.en: At the banquet, warmed with wine, everyone was fired with passion.

examples.zh: 这首诗慨当以慷，满怀家国之情。
examples.en: The poem is impassioned and full of feeling for nation and home.

story.en: Cao Cao's 'Short Song': 'Our song is stirring and impassioned, and the worries in my heart cannot be forgotten' (慨当以慷，忧思难忘).
story.zh: 曹操《短歌行》：“慨当以慷，忧思难忘。何以解忧，唯有杜康。”

usage.en: Do not read it word by word: 慨当以慷 is an old way of saying 慷慨, 'stirring and passionate'. Literary, tied to Cao Cao's poem.
usage.zh: 不能逐字理解：“慨当以慷”是“慷慨”的古式说法，指情绪激昂。书面语，与曹操诗相关。

natural: a bright and clear world

meaning.en: A clean, well-ordered world under the rule of law; used to protest wrongdoing: how can this happen under such a bright sky?
meaning.zh: 清明的天下，太平盛世；常用于质问：在这样清明的世界里怎能有此恶行。

equivalents: in broad daylight, in a just world
under clear skies and the rule of law

examples.zh: 朗朗乾坤，岂容坏人横行？
examples.en: In this bright and orderly world, how could villains be allowed to run wild?

examples.zh: 朗朗乾坤之下，不允许有任何违法乱纪。
examples.en: Under a bright and well-ordered world, no lawbreaking is tolerated.

examples.zh: 要还社会一个朗朗乾坤。
examples.en: We must give society back a clean and orderly world.

usage.en: Often in rhetorical questions of indignation, or in officialese about a healthy society; 朗朗 repeats 'bright'. Like 光天化日 but more solemn.
usage.zh: 常见于愤慨的反问，或官方语言中谈清朗社会；“朗朗”叠用，意为明亮。与“光天化日”相近但更庄重。

natural: a dewdrop couple

meaning.en: An unmarried couple living together briefly, an affair with no lasting bond.
meaning.zh: 没有正式婚姻关系、短暂同居的男女，像露水一样不能长久。

examples.zh: 他们只是露水夫妻，谁也没想过长久。
examples.en: They were just a temporary couple and neither thought of lasting.

examples.zh: 小说里写了一对露水夫妻的聚散。
examples.en: The novel tells of a transient couple's meetings and partings.

examples.zh: 别把露水夫妻当真，感情经不起考验。
examples.en: Don't take a fleeting liaison seriously; such feelings can't stand the test.

usage.en: Mildly derogatory and informal; avoid it about real people. Usually found in fiction, also 露水姻缘.
usage.zh: 略带贬义，较随便；对真人不宜用。多见于小说，也说“露水姻缘”。

natural: the style of a celebrated scholar

meaning.en: The unrestrained elegance and charm of a talented literatus.
meaning.zh: 有名的文人才子不拘小节、洒脱风雅的气度。

equivalents: the carefree style of a gifted scholar

examples.zh: 他性情洒脱，颇有名士风流。
examples.en: He is free-spirited and has a good deal of the carefree style of a literatus.

examples.zh: 魏晋名士风流，饮酒作诗，不拘礼法。
examples.en: The Wei-Jin scholars were free and stylish, drinking and writing poems with no regard for convention.

examples.zh: 她爱好书画，别有一番名士风流。
examples.en: She loves calligraphy and painting, with a literatus's elegance of her own.

usage.en: Admiring; strongly linked with the Wei and Jin dynasties' Seven Sages and the idea of unconventional charm. Often 名士风度.
usage.zh: 带欣赏意味；与魏晋七贤和不拘一格的风度密切相关。也说“名士风度”。

natural: sift sand to pick out gold

meaning.en: To select the best from a great mass of material; work hard to extract what is valuable.
meaning.zh: 从沙子中拣出金子，比喻从大量材料中筛选精华。

equivalents: sift the wheat from the chaff

examples.zh: 编辑要披沙拣金，从海量来稿中选出好文章。
examples.en: An editor must sift through the heap to pick the good pieces from the flood of submissions.

examples.zh: 研究古籍就像披沙拣金，耐心最重要。
examples.en: Studying ancient books is like panning for gold; patience matters most.

examples.zh: 网络信息太多，需要披沙拣金的能力。
examples.en: There's so much online that you need the ability to pick out what counts.

usage.en: Positive; about selection and screening, with an implication of painstaking effort. 沙里淘金 is the colloquial form.
usage.zh: 褒义；指选择和筛选，含费心费力之意。口语中常说“沙里淘金”。

natural: a seven-foot body

meaning.en: The body of a grown man (seven chi in ancient measure); often 'as a full-grown man'.
meaning.zh: 指成年男子的身体（古代七尺）；常用“堂堂七尺之躯”。

examples.zh: 我堂堂七尺之躯，岂能受此侮辱？
examples.en: I'm a grown man; how could I suffer such an insult?

examples.zh: 他愿以七尺之躯报效国家。
examples.en: He is willing to give his life in the service of his country.

examples.zh: 七尺之躯，岂可为五斗米折腰？
examples.en: A grown man, should he bow for five dou of rice?

usage.en: Literary; speaker often uses it of himself for dignity or to declare self-sacrifice. Also 七尺男儿, 七尺须眉.
usage.zh: 书面语；常用于自称，表示尊严或牺牲决心。也说“七尺男儿”“七尺须眉”。
